title: GRAFT introduces execution-guided genetic recombination for LLM agent design
summary: A research preprint introduced GRAFT, an evolutionary search framework for LLM agent architectures that steers semantic crossover using parent execution traces rather than aggregate fitness scores alone, reporting improved reasoning and coding benchmark performance on open-weight models.
research_notes:
Define the candidate agent search space, specifying allowable prompt templates, decomposition steps, and coordination protocols for target tasks.

Execute parent architectures on evaluation benchmarks to collect both scalar performance scores and sample execution logs recording successes and failures.

Select parent candidates by aggregate fitness, then construct recombination prompts that present parent code alongside their bounded execution traces.

Prompt the recombination LLM to synthesize offspring agent designs that retain successful execution behaviors and mutate failing components without exposing gold answers.

Recycle execution traces from standard fitness evaluations rather than executing auxiliary inference runs to keep search compute bounded.

Maintain strict separation between intermediate execution traces and ground-truth labels during crossover prompts to avoid benchmark overfitting and test leakage.

Retain aggregate fitness for top-level tournament selection while restricting execution-guided feedback strictly to crossover and mutation operators.
